findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on file read failure
findings.failure_mode: missing or unreadable file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and propagate with ? or map_err at the boundary

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on malformed input or out-of-range value
findings.failure_mode: a single non-numeric or oversized field in the CSV aborts the entire session load instead of reporting a typed Parse or Value error
findings.fix: use .split(',') with checked indexing (split_once or get), call parse with map_err to a typed ParseError, and validate the u32 fits in u16 before casting

findings.problem: lossy as cast from u32 to u16: (.parse::<u32>().unwrap()) as u16 silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value of 70000 becomes 4463 without any error, corrupting the domain data
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32) or validate with .checked_into::<u16>() and return a typed Value error on overflow

findings.problem: parts[0] unchecked indexing into split result without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: a line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields triggers a panic at runtime
findings.fix: use line.split_once(',') or iterate with enumerate and guard on len < 2, returning a typed Parse error

findings.problem: parts[1] unchecked indexing into split result without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: same as above — any line missing the second field panics
findings.fix: use split_once(',') to get exactly two parts, or validate .len() >= 2 before indexing

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with data parsing in a single public function
findings.failure_mode: the pure parsing logic cannot be tested in isolation; I/O failure modes are tangled with domain parsing errors; no deterministic unit tests possible for the parser
findings.fix: split into (a) a pure fn parse_session_line(line: &str) -> Result<Record, ParseError> for the core, and (b) a shell fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError> that calls read_to_string, iterates lines, and delegates to parse_session_line

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) is a hidden side effect inside a data-processing function
findings.failure_mode: logging couples the core to a concrete output target, makes the function non-deterministic in output, prevents silent testing, and violates the rule that only the shell may perform side effects
findings.fix: remove println entirely from the core; if progress reporting is needed, expose it via a callback or builder pattern in the shell layer

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no error type — all failures are expressed as panics
findings.failure_mode: callers have no way to distinguish file-not-found, parse errors, value-out-of-range, or malformed-line errors; the error taxonomy is entirely missing
findings.fix: define a SessionError enum with variants (Io(io::Error), Parse(ParseError), Value(ValueError)) and return Result<Vec<Record>, SessionError>

findings.problem: Vec<String> allocation from split without try_reserve or capacity hint
findings.failure_mode: malformed lines with many commas can cause unbounded heap allocations, enabling allocation-based DoS
findings.fix: compute expected capacity from line.len(), call try_reserve before the map/collect chain, and map allocation failure to an Allocation error

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim
no profiler data (cargo flamegraph, perf, or similar) for the parsing path
no allocation analysis (e.g., allocs per line, total allocation budget)
no second-ring evidence: no Miri UB check, no Kani bounded verification, no property tests
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. All error paths are panic-exit with zero error taxonomy, lossy casts, unchecked indexing, hidden I/O side effects in the core, and no bounded allocation. This crate is not Holzman-compliant and should not be delivered without the structural splits, typed errors, checked arithmetic, and removed forbidden constructs.
